ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions lists, and the Central Bank of Cyprus sanctioned persons list; PEP status determined under Law 188(I)/2007. Enhanced due diligence applies to any PEP, family member or close associate. Additional OFAC SDN List screening is standard market practice for opening correspondent banking accounts in USD. Continuous monitoring via World-Check or equivalent is required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ariadne Online Portal, Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver, Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in Greek or Latin (English) characters; when a name is in Greek, a Latin transliteration must be filed for EU-level cross-checks. The corporate suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd' (or its Greek equivalent 'Λτδ') is mandatory. Transliteration into the Greek alphabet is required for any foreign name to ensure safe search and publication in the Cyprus Gazette.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or their counsel must file a written administrative appeal to the Registrar of Companies within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include the proposed name, the registry file reference, a legal memorandum on compliance with Cap. 113 and special licensing regulations, and any supporting authorisations for sensitive tokens. The Registrar typically issues a decision within 30 days. If the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may challenge the decision before the District Court under Article 146 of the Constitution within 75 days of the final rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is accepted for registered correspondence but the physical registered address must be in Cyprus and receive mail. For a social-casino software publisher, no CySEC licence is required, but a physical office or co-working space is recommended to support VAT registration, banking (including Apple IAP/Google Play merchant accounts), and commercial substance. Pure virtual offices may be challenged under substance requirements when relying on income tax benefits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (5% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection by the Registrar or tax authorities when the company is small, non-licensed, and filing accurate returns)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law, Cap 113 (Republic of Cyprus), as amended; ss. 3 and 4 (incorporation and memorandum/articles), ss. 16-26 (share capital), ss. 113-135 (officers and registered office); Beneficial Owners Register Law 133(I)/2021; Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) as applied in Cyprus
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DROCOR), Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, Nicosia, Cyprus
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association filed with the Incorporation Application (Form HE1); issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the HE registration number
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by Cap 113; at least one fully paid ordinary share of EUR 1.00 must be issued. No escrow or blocked capital deposit is required by the Registrar; for banking substance a nominal authorised capital of EUR 1,000 divided into ordinary shares of EUR 1.00 is customary, with only the issued portion paid up.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the subscription for one fully-paid ordinary share by the incorporating shareholder be and it is hereby accepted and allotted, the consideration being satisfied as recorded in the register of members; (2) that the registered office of the Company be and it is hereby fixed at the address set out in the Articles of Association and the Registrar of Companies shall be notified accordingly; (3) that [Name] be and is hereby appointed first director, that [Name] be appointed secretary, and that their respective Consents to Act shall be filed; (4) that the first director is authorized to open banking accounts, execute documents, and procure payment of all incorporation fees and Government charges; and (5) that all prior incorporation acts are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search and Availability Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DROCOR e-Registry (online name availability index), Department of Registrar of Companies, Nicosia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-filing name search in the DROCOR e-Registry to ascertain that the proposed name 'CY LTD' is not identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered name. Confirm the name is in Latin characters, contains the eligible suffix 'Ltd', and does not include restricted or prohibited words. Reserve the name electronically; the reservation is automatically linked to the incorporation application when lodged within the reservation validity window.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and transliteration confirmation
Draft Memorandum of Association containing the name clause and objects clause (ISIC 5820 software publishing)
Power of attorney executed in favour of the incorporation agent
Name availability search report from DROCOR e-Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as identical or confusingly similar, file a written Name Objection/Appeal with DROCOR under Cap 113 supported by trademark registration or prior-user evidence, or submit an amended incorporation request with an alternative proposed name within 14 days of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents and Share Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cyprus notary public and licensed fiduciary agents; interim review by DROCOR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in accordance with Cap 113 and the Table B model, including the objects clause limited to publishing and licensing of simulated social casino and virtual slots software for mobile platforms. Execute the subscriber decision allotting one ordinary share of EUR 1.00 to the incorporating shareholder. Obtain executed Consent to Act forms from the first director and secretary. Notarize and apostille all documents executed outside Cyprus in compliance with the Hague Convention 1961.
required_dossiers: Drafted and paginated Memorandum and Articles of Association
Subscriber decision / share subscription and allotment record
Consent to Act forms of first director and secretary
Certified passport copies and proof of residential address of all subscribers
Notarized and apostilled board/subscriber forms for non-resident signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DROCOR requires rectification, translation into Greek, or additional legalization of foreign executed documents, submit the corrected or translated instrument through the designated Cyprus agent within 10 business days; pay the applicable rectification stamp duty of EUR 20 per page set where mandated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application with DROCOR and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DROCOR), Nicosia filing window and e-Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the certified Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Incorporation Application Form HE1 and the signed consents through the DROCOR e-Registry. Pay the statutory incorporation fee and native government charges using the DROCOR approved payment rails. After verification of statutory compliance, receive the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the HE registration number and the official seal of the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Completed Form HE1 incorporation application
Certified copy of Memorandum and Articles of Association
Executed Consent to Act forms of first director and secretary
Registered office consent letter from the property owner or managing agent
Receipt of payment of the EUR 155 statutory incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Registrar issues a Notice of Query, remedy the formal deficiency within 14 days by filing a supplementary affidavit or corrected form; if the statutory fee is underpaid, settle the difference with additional stamp duty and a penalty of EUR 50 before re-submission. Unresolved queries after 14 days require a fresh filing and another fee payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Corporate Governance Filings and Registered Office Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DROCOR; Tax Department of the Republic of Cyprus; Registrar of Beneficial Ownership
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the company statutory registers (members, directors, secretaries, charges) at the registered office; file particulars of the first director, secretary, and registered office with DROCOR; obtain the Tax Identification Code (TIC) from the Tax Department; lodge the Beneficial Ownership Register return identifying the ultimate beneficial owner; if the company processes personal data, notify the Office of the Commissioner for Personal Data Protection of the data controller status.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and HE registration number
Register of members and register of directors and secretaries
Registered office notification form filed with DROCOR
Beneficial Ownership Register filing with UBO details
TIC application form with certified constitutional documents
Data controller registration form under GDPR Article 30 where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any omission in the Beneficial Ownership Register immediately upon notice to avoid the EUR 200 per day penalty regime; late TIC applications may be expedited by a written justification letter to the Tax Department. Duplicate filings will be corrected by the Registrar's administrative revision procedure without additional court involvement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, Social Insurance and Banking Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tax Department (Nicosia District Office); Social Insurance Services; commercial banking institution (AML/KYC desk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for Cyprus income tax under the TIC obtained in Step 4. Register for VAT in Cyprus when taxable turnover exceeds the statutory threshold of EUR 13,500, or alternatively apply for voluntary VAT registration in order to recover input VAT on Apple IAP and Google Play Billing intermediary fees. Register as an employer with the Social Insurance Services and open the corporate bank account, submitting the first board resolution authorizing signatories and the AML/KYC file of all directors and ultimate beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: TIC registration certificate and Certificate of Incorporation
VAT registration form (Form VTC17) or voluntary VAT application
Social Insurance employer registration with the SIP payroll schedule
Corporate resolution on bank signatories and account mandates
AML/KYC pack comprising passport, proof of address, source of funds, and corporate structure chart
Pro forma publishing agreement or app store developer account statement for commercial substance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank rejects the KYC file, submit alternative source-of-funds evidence or appoint a local independent director to strengthen substance; if VAT registration is delayed, file a voluntary disclosure with the Tax Department within 30 days to regularize the effective date and mitigate penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Premises, Municipal Operating Licence and Occupational Safety Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipality Licensing Committee; Fire Service (Cyprus Fire Brigade); Department of Labour Inspection, Ministry of Labour, Welfare and Social Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure a lease for the registered office and working premises and obtain the landlord's written consent. Submit the municipal commercial operating licence application with certified company documents, the lease, and the premises layout plan. Coordinate a fire safety inspection and obtain the Fire Safety Risk Assessment and, where triggers apply, the Fire Safety Certificate for the premises and any server/IT rack room. Notify the Department of Labour Inspection of workplace occupation and employees, and certify a compliant workplace risk assessment.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement and landlord consent letter for municipal licensing
Municipal commercial operating licence application form
Premises layout drawings and fire escape plan
Fire safety risk assessment prepared by a certified assessor
Structural load verification certificate for the server room floor
Workplace risk assessment and first-aid/emergency equipment inventory
Certificate of Incorporation and director identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal licence application is queried, submit supplementary compliance certificates (electrical installation certificate, structural engineer's note, revised fire escape plan) within 10 business days; a formal refusal may be appealed to the Municipal Committee under the Municipalities Law. Fire safety deficiencies must be remedied and re-inspected before the certificate is issued; the Department of Labour Inspection may issue improvement notices with a 21-day compliance deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Licensing Committee of the registered office municipality; Cyprus Fire Brigade; Department of Labour Inspection (Ministry of Labour, Welfare and Social Insurance); Department of Environment (Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Commercial and Business Premises Operating Licence. Statutory licensing note: the simulated social casino and virtual slots publishing model is a non-real-money wagering activity and is therefore outside the scope of the Republic of Cyprus betting and gambling licensing regime; no Cyprus Betting Authority licence, casino licence, or CySEC gaming authorisation is required for the CY_LTD scope as filed.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment, Republic of Cyprus
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - No EIA Required. Office-based software publishing is not listed in Annex I or Annex II of the Environmental Impact Assessment Law 127(I)/2018; the activity is de minimis and requires only standard waste segregation and WEEE compliance registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or combustion-related emissions arise. Sanitary effluent is discharged solely to the central municipal sewerage network under the local Sewerage Boards Law. Waste electrical and electronic equipment (obsolete servers, IT equipment) must be handled in accordance with Law 185(I)/2011 transposing Directive 2012/19/EU, and rechargeable battery waste under the Batteries Law. Refrigerant quantities in HVAC systems remain below the F-Gas Regulation de minimis thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Risk Assessment endorsed by the Cyprus Fire Brigade and, where the premises exceed the statutory occupancy threshold, a Fire Safety Certificate; structural load verification for the server/IT rack area; workplace risk assessment, first-aid and emergency evacuation measures compliant with the Safety and Health at Work Act 89(I)/1996 and the Minimum Requirements for Workplaces Directive.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Department of Taxation of the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Cyprus (Nicosia); taxpayer portal: ARIADE (Tax For All) at ariade.mof.gov.cy; official tax department website: www.mof.gov.cy/taxdep.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Cyprus private limited company (HE prefix): the company is incorporated with the Registrar of Companies and the Department of Taxation automatically issues a Tax Identification Number (TIN) that mirrors the HE registration number; no separate income tax registration is needed. A foreign-owned company that will make taxable supplies in Cyprus must file Form VAT-1 through the ARIADE portal, declaring anticipated CY taxable turnover, or register under the Union OSS / non-Union schemes for cross-border electronic services. Mandatory VAT registration is required within 30 days of exceeding the EUR 15,600 annual threshold; voluntary registration is available for the export-oriented game publisher. Non-resident companies with no Cyprus fixed establishment may be registered directly or through a tax representative in Cyprus.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - Cyprus private limited company is taxed as the liable taxable person at 12.5% corporate income tax; no pass-through or transparency is permitted, and a modified territoriality exemption applies to foreign dividends and foreign permanent establishment profits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Cyprus has no check-the-box regime, but offers statutory elections: (i) deemed-dividend distribution election under Income Tax Law section 37 (17% special defence contribution on the distribution of otherwise undistributed profits); (ii) Notional Interest Deduction (NID) election on new equity capital introduced after 1 January 2015; (iii) IP Box regime election (80% tax deduction on qualifying IP profits); (iv) group loss relief and group gain elections; (v) VAT OSS/IOSS and EC Sales List election schemes; and (vi) hybrid-mismatch elections and disclosures required under the EU ATAD provisions as implemented in Cyprus.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Cyprus Value Added Tax) governed by the Value Added Tax Law 2000 (N.95(I)/2000)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 15,600 annual taxable turnover of supplies of goods and services with a place of supply in Cyprus (mandatory registration within 30 days of the threshold being reached); EUR 10,000 annual remote intra-EU distance sales threshold for micro-businesses.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API e-invoicing or digital stamping is currently in force in Cyprus. Electronic invoices are accepted on equal footing with paper invoices under the VAT Law, provided authenticity, integrity and legibility are preserved. Cyprus is aligning with the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package: a mandatory EU-wide B2B e-invoicing and digital reporting framework is expected by 2030; Cypriot businesses should maintain e-invoicing capability for Apple IAP and Google Play Billing ledgers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating (0%) applies to (i) exports of goods physically dispatched or transported to a non-EU destination; (ii) intra-Community supplies of goods to a business customer holding a valid EU VAT identification number and reported in the EC Sales List; and (iii) international transport services and ancillary loading services. Electronic services (social casino games, virtual slots) supplied to non-EU B2C consumers fall outside the scope of Cypriot VAT under the place-of-supply rules rather than being zero-rated; supplies to EU B2C consumers are taxed in the consumer's Member State via the OSS scheme, and B2B supplies to foreign businesses are reverse-charged. The exporter must retain conclusive evidence that goods left the EU within the statutory time frame and that the economic benefit accrued to the Cypriot entity. No Cyprus statutory foreign-exchange repatriation period is codified, but the mandated 180-day window in this dossier is used as the bank compliance benchmark for inward remittances from Apple IAP and Google Play.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Single Administrative Document) with exported Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Commercial invoice and proforma or contract evidencing the export sale
Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note or Air Waybill proving physical departure from the European Union
Packing list and customs or port arrival proofs where requested
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank swift or credit confirmation linking payment to the specific export transaction
Customer's valid EU VAT number and EC Sales List / VIES confirmation for intra-Community supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Department of Taxation may assess VAT at 19% where zero-rating is claimed without an adequate documentary trail, with a correction period normally of five years from filing (no time limit in fraud cases), plus statutory interest and administrative penalties under Article 53 of the VAT Law. Deliberate fraudulent zero-rating claims attract criminal prosecution, fines (up to EUR 15,000), imprisonment (up to three years), retrospective clawback of input VAT, revocation of approved exporter status, and publication of penalties. Approved economic operators are subject to continuing customs and VAT audits; the social casino publisher's Apple IAP and Google Play remittance records are included in the audit perimeter.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Cyprus (Kεντρική Τράπεζα της Κύπρου) as the national competent authority within the Eurosystem, with the European Central Bank (ECB) as the ultimate monetary and foreign exchange policy authority for euro-area members
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Cyprus, as a euro-area member state, maintains full currency convertibility. Both current and capital account transactions are unrestricted under the EU Capital Movement Directive (Directive 88/361/EEC) and the Cypriot Exchange Control Law framework, which has been effectively suspended/abolished since EU accession (2004). Profit remittances, dividends, capital repatriation, and loan servicing may be freely executed via licensed credit institutions without prior central bank or ministry approval, subject only to standard anti-money laundering ('AML') due diligence, tax withholding compliance (where applicable), and international sanctions screening. Restrictions would only arise from EU/UN sanctions, judicial orders, or a bank's internal risk appetite. No general convertibility hurdles or material profit remittance impediments exist for a Cyprus private limited company in good standing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Cyprus imposes no statutory obligation to surrender export proceeds, no mandatory conversion of foreign currency receipts into EUR, and no specified timeline for repatriation of export earnings. Export proceeds may be held in foreign-currency accounts, retained abroad for treasury purposes, or converted at market rates, subject to bank-level account monitoring, intra-EU customs documentation, and VIES/Intrastat reporting where applicable. For reasonableness, banks may apply internal guidelines requiring supporting invoices/Bill of Lading to justify large inbound credits.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for treasury facilitation, but not a substitute for a licensed commercial bank settlement account. Cyprus-licensed and EEA passported Electronic Money Institutions are permissible under the Electronic Money Law (L.87(I)/2012) and PSD2, and may provide multi-currency IBANs, low-cost payment collection, FX conversion, and enhanced payment API integration for social-casino revenue flows (Apple/Google payouts). However, offshore digital EMIs from non-EEA jurisdictions without a Central Bank of Cyprus passport or EU equivalent cannot lawfully provide payment services to Cypriot entities; using such unfinancially regulated entities would constitute an AML red flag and likely breach local licensing rules for payment services. For capital escrow and large trade settlements, a regulated Tier-1 bank remains mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors must appear physically only if the onboarding bank's risk-based approach demands it, notably for non-resident or high-risk beneficial owners, complex ownership structures, or significant non-EEA counterparty exposure. Cyprus AML statute permits remote/video identification in accordance with an EU-compliant video-identification procedure and the Central Bank's AML Directive, provided the bank uses a certified system and records are retained. In practice, leading banks (Bank of Cyprus, Hellenic) routinely require either physical attendance of at least one local director/authorised signatory at a branch, or a video interview supplemented by apostilled corporate documents, original passports, and recent utility bills. A local corporate service provider ('CSP') having an existing banking relationship may substantially ease remote-opening feasibility.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Social casino / casual gaming sector classified as 'Enhanced Risk' under sector-specific AML typologies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full legal opinion confirming the platform offers no real-money gambling, slots or sweepstakes with zero cash redemption; certified game rules and terms of service; age-verification and geo-restriction controls; anti-fraud and responsible-gaming policy; Apple/Google publisher agreements; audited financial statements projecting revenue disaggregation; a clear AML risk assessment for the business model; and a written explanation of how end-user deposits/withdrawals are segregated from operating treasury flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner or opaque offshore shareholding chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate register extracts (Cyprus Companies Registry), an up-to-date beneficial ownership declaration filed under the Central Register of Beneficial Owners, notarised passports and proof of residential address for all UBOs holding ≥10%, a bank reference letter from the UBO's home jurisdiction, source-of-wealth statement supported by tax returns or audited accounts, and a formal corporate structure chart explaining each intermediate entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual inbound capital injection, e.g., crypto-denominated or from unrelated high-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed shareholders' resolution approving the capital increase; SWIFT MT103/MT202 trail showing the originating bank; source-of-funds documentation comprising sale-and-purchase agreements, inheritance/divestment records, or lending agreements; crypto exchange statements and wallet-chain analysis if any portion of the inward remittance passed through digital assets; tax clearances from both the sending jurisdiction and Cyprus; and a letter of undertaking to provide ongoing transaction transparency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Misalignment between the registered business object (ISIC 5820 software publishing) and the actual payment rails or FX volumes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan mapping ISIC 5820 to predicted traffic, throughputs and settlement cycles; app-store performance dashboards; licensing agreements for software/IP; customer and vendor instruments; transaction-flow diagrams showing where the entity receives and pays funds; and legal counsel's analysis confirming that social casino/non-gambling software publishing is consistent with Article 2 of the Cyprus Companies Law and the Priority of Payments under bank account terms.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing uses a single-leg or dual-leg SWIFT MT103/MT202 TT from the investor's bank to the Cyprus account, with the payment purpose coded as 'CAPT' (capital contribution) or 'MCNE' (equity injection), and a beneficiary reference containing the company name and project code. The receiving Cyprus bank will require a certified board/shareholder resolution authorising the capital increase, an updated Companies Registry extract reflecting the issued share capital, an AML/beneficial ownership declaration, and evidence of source of funds. The transfer must be free from sanctions-tainted jurisdictions and should be accompanied by a formal currency conversion instruction if the investor holds non-EUR funds. For amounts exceeding EUR 100,000, the bank will also conduct a false-prescriptive vetting under the Central Bank's AML directives. Capital injections are not subject to Cypriot exchange-control approval, but may trigger stamp-duty or capital duty obligations (if applicable, assessable on nominal share capital), and should be reported in the next annual financial statements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for cross-border vendor, royalty, and licensing payments originating from the Cyprus operational account. For EUR-denominated trade within the SEPA zone (including Apple/Google Ireland counterparts), SEPA Instant Payment/SCT is preferred for low-value, same-day treasury execution. For high-value or documentary trade settlements (purchase of ad inventory, software white-label agreements, payment-processor commissions), Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) may be used where a supplier demands banking-security arrangements. All outbound payments should include a clear business purpose code, the underlying invoice reference or contract number, and be vetted against the bank's sanctions list; payments to non-EEA beneficiaries require a completed KYC questionnaire for the counterparty, and for recurring payouts, the bank may ask for a standing-payment-authorisation mandate signed by two directors.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/TRY and other exotic deliverable forwards, subject to available country depth and credit line
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or inconvertible currencies used for emerging-market treasury payments, if legal and bank-approved
Cross-currency swaps (EUR vs USD/GBP) for balance-sheet hedging of loan/exposure mismatches
European-style vanilla over-the-counter options (FX calls/puts) in major currencies, executed under an ISDA 2002/CSA master agreement where required by the crypto-horizon bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Intellectual Property (DRCIP), Nicosia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days of the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers administrative penalties; continued non-payment or non-filing for six months may lead to administrative strike-off and dissolution. Restoration requires court order and reinstatement fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a fixed penalty of EUR 50 plus default interest; prolonged non-payment for six months or more may trigger administrative strike-off and loss of good-standing certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days of every change in beneficial ownership, including any share transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is a continuing offence exposing the company and responsible officers to daily administrative fines up to EUR 200 and criminal penalties; persistent default may be treated as grounds for strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for every active Cyprus private limited company. The dormant-company exemption under Companies Law Cap. 113 applies only where the company has performed no accounting transactions; an active social-casino publisher with digital revenue is ineligible for exemption and must appoint an ICPAC-licensed auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards as adopted by the European Union (EU-IFRS); Cyprus has no separate domestic generally accepted accounting principles.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Cyprus does not require a standalone calendar-year UBO form. On each share transfer, the internal register of beneficial owners must be updated on the transfer date, and an amended UBO return must be filed with DRCIP within 14 days. The annual HE32 return must be reconciled with the current members register.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Cyprus applies a flat corporate income tax rate of 12.5% on worldwide taxable income for tax-resident companies. Notional interest deduction (NID) on new equity capital (subject to conditions, capped at 80% of taxable income). IP Box regime (per OECD Nexus approach) allowing 80% deduction on qualifying intangible income, resulting in an effective rate of 2.5% on such income (with grandfathering and grandfathering rules as amended). Tonnage tax regime for qualifying shipping activities (not applicable to software/gaming).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form TD201 (Cypriot Corporation Tax Return) filed electronically via the Tax For All (TFA) online portal operated by the Tax Department of the Republic of Cyprus (εφορία / Tax Department).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 15 months after the end of the tax year (i.e., for a company with a 31 December fiscal year-end, deadline is 31 March of the second following year, but tax must be paid by 31 December of the current income year in two provisional instalments: 31 July and 31 December).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification details (name, tax identification code, registration number, registered office address).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the full legal name exactly as registered with the Registrar of Companies and the Cyprus Tax Identification Code (TIC) or VAT number; foreign address must be provided if no Cyprus registered office is maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the fiscal period covered by the return; for a non-resident company with a permanent establishment in Cyprus, use the PE accounting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit for the accounting period before tax adjustments, as per audited financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident company must report only Cyprus-sourced income attributable to the Cyprus permanent establishment (PE); provide the PE's separate branch accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disallowable expenses and non-deductible items (e.g., non-wholly-wholly expenses, depreciation adjustments, bribes/penalties).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate disallowable expenses to the Cyprus PE under the force of attraction principle; deduct only expenses economically connected with the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit computation add-backs and exempt income deductions (e.g., dividend income exemption, interest from bond debentures, IP Box deduction).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the Cyprus-sourced exempt income rules; non-resident companies may only claim exemptions attributable to PE income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward and tax loss relief claimed from previous years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses from foreign activities of a non-resident with a Cyprus PE cannot be set off against Cyprus PE income unless the foreign loss is Cyprus-sourced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Chargeable income subject to corporate income tax (taxable profits after adjustments and reliefs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Cyprus PE's taxable income under the separate-entity approach.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax payable at 12.5% (after NID, tax credits and foreign tax relief).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies cannot claim the NID unless the qualifying equity capital is allocated to the PE; foreign tax credit only for tax paid on Cyprus PE income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration and signature block (legal representative / professional tax adviser).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Cyprus PE's authorised representative or the appointed local tax agent must sign.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission penalty: EUR 100 (increased to EUR 200 for each outstanding tax return) for any outstanding return; administrative fine of EUR 100 per return; interest at 1.75% per quarter (or as revised annually by Ministerial Decree) on unpaid tax; criminal sanctions in case of fraudulent filing or deliberate evasion: up to 5 years imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding EUR 3,000 for individuals, and for companies a fine up to EUR 30,000. Also, imposition of 'additional charge' of 10% on late-paid tax and 5% surcharge for late provisional tax instalments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Cyprus does not impose withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents, including Cyprus resident companies and non-resident shareholders, subject to Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive (ATAD) and EU Anti-BEPS rules).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: As Cyprus does not impose withholding tax on outgoing dividends under domestic law, no treaty relief procedure is required for dividends. For royalties and interest, the zero or reduced treaty rate is activated by delivery of a Cyprus Tax Residence Certificate (TRC issued by the Tax Department), a DTA application form (usually Form IR 850 or individually prescribed TRC format), supporting beneficial ownership declaration, and submission to the Cyprus tax authorities by the withholding agent/payer for issuance of a reduced-rate directive or confirmatory letter before payment; updated TRCs are generally valid for a calendar year and must be provided to the Cypriot payer prior to any payment to avoid gross-basis withholding or to obtain refund of excess withholding via the Cyprus Structural Funds/Withholding Tax Refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT: Cyprus does not impose withholding tax on royalties or interest paid to non-residents under domestic law. However, Cyprus applies a 10% special contribution for defence (SDC) on interest accrued for the benefit of Cyprus-resident individuals (not companies); non-residents are exempt from SDC. Under the Income Tax Law, a deemed distribution of profits is subject to SDC at 17% (or 15% in some cases) for Cyprus-resident shareholders. Treaty rates: under Cyprus DTAs (e.g., Cyprus–UK, Cyprus–Luxembourg, Cyprus–UAE and most EU/EEA treaties), dividends generally 0% (some 5%/15%), interest 0% or 10% (many 0% under EU parent-subsidiary), royalties 0% or up to 10% (e.g., Cyprus–Russia 5% royalty rate under historical treaty; EU treaties 0% under Interest & Royalties Directive where applicable, limiting WHT to 0% on related-company interest/royalty payments).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000 (annual intercompany transactions of goods, services, royalties or loans for local file preparation), and Master File required when Group aggregate turnover exceeds EUR 75,000,000 and intercompany transactions exceed the threshold prescribed by administrative practice; Cyprus TP rules (s. 51 Income Tax Law, Defence Law, and Administrative Guidelines) align with OECD TPG, and documentation is compulsory when the transaction value exceeds EUR 750,000 per category or when the enterprise operates 'high-value' intangible and financing arrangements; smaller firms must still prepare contemporaneous TP documentation in case of audit, as penalties apply even without threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Cyprus has implemented Economic Substance Rules under the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive 1 (ATAD) via the Interpretation Guidelines and the Cyprus Income Tax Law; all Cyprus-resident companies (including tax-exempt entities) that derive relevant income (or have assets and risk) from IP, financing, leasing, or high-risk functions must demonstrate real economic activity commensurate with the business: physical premises, qualified full-time employees (appropriately senior to decision-making), actual board meetings in Cyprus, and local management discretion. The rules are primarily triggered for entities holding IP assets or performing intellectual property functions; in a social-casino/gaming holding structure generating digital royalties or management fees, absence of such substance creates a fatal red flag. The Cypriot authorities apply the OECD/EFTA approach and require detailed local substance documentation, substance reports, annual evidence of bank activity and management minutes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately filing false or truncated corporate tax returns underreporting revenue from in-app purchases (Apple IAP / Google Play Billing) or concealing Cyprus-sourced project income; artificial misclassification of revenue as capital receipts; using shell invoice companies outside Cyprus without commercial substance to divert profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Cyprus Income Tax Law s.93 and Criminal Code, conviction renders imprisonment up to 5 years and/or fine up to EUR 3,000 for individuals; corporate fine up to EUR 30,000; additional tax assessment at 100% of the deficient tax plus interest at 1.75% per quarter and a statutory penalty up to EUR 3,000 per false return; publication/reputation sanctions under anti-money laundering framework.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil where the company is a mere façade and director controls routing of payments; directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes under registration/collection orders if they signed fraudulent returns or are involved in the preparation of falsified accounts; civil restitution orders, travel bans (departure prohibition orders issued by tax authorities), disqualification as director (up to 10 years), and personal criminal liability can attach even for limited-liability companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mismatch / Absence of Arm's Length File
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cyprus entity inaccurately prices licensing royalties, management fees, or interest payments to foreign associated enterprises; failing to maintain local file/master file when intercompany transactions exceed EUR 750,000; setting transfer pricing without functional analysis or expected economic return for the social-casino game rights; undocumented profit shifting to zero-tax jurisdictions via inflated royalty payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Authority may upward adjust taxable profits by the arm's length deviation, impose additional tax at 12.5% with interest at 1.75% per quarter (or current quarterly rate) and administrative penalties of up to EUR 5,000 for missing/incorrect documentation; in serious cases, criminal prosecution for tax evasion with imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving non-arm's length arrangements without documented board rationale and economic substance may be held jointly liable for penalty tax, and their actions may trigger the reverse onus of proof in tax fraud proceedings; personal asset freezing or worldwide freezing orders are available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: CY Ltd is a registered recipient of profits from mobile game publishing (ISIC 5820) with no employees, no office, no local servers, no real decision-making in Cyprus, and all strategic functions exercised by a foreign parent; treated as a conduit that receives IP or game revenue but passes funds abroad without the requisite connection to physical operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cyprus Directorate of Tax and Customs may disregard the company's taxable presence and re-assess profits to the beneficial owner under the Anti-Avoidance Rules (s.61A Income Tax Law, section 66/67 AAD); penalties include denial of treaty benefits (under MLI and DTA abuse limitation), issuance of a 'special assessment' with 5% monthly penalties (capped at 50%), and revocation of tax residence certificate; if the company enters insolvency, there is no limited-liability protection and creditors/authorities can apply for striking-off and disqualification orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be subject to loss of limited liability for wrongful trading, personal liability for tax debts under s. 48 of the Companies Law, Cap. 113 (if distributions were made while insolvent), and criminal sanctions for operating a company as a vehicle of fraud; additional 'official liquidator' investigations may lead to 12-year restriction orders and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting payments via Apple IAP / Google Play Billing for social-casino virtual chips without robust know-your-customer (KYC) and sanctions screening; handling proceeds traceable to fraudulent or unlawful gaming transactions; facilitating anonymous in-app transfers that circumvent the Prevention and Suppression of Money Laundering Activities Law (L.188(I)/2007).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cyprus Unit for Combating Money Laundering (MOKAS) may impose administrative penalties up to EUR 200,000 or 5% of annual turnover (under AML Directive implementation), criminal fine for money laundering to EUR 100,000 or imprisonment up to 10 years; assets may be forfeited under Section 3 and 4 of the AML Law; CySEC (if auxiliary services provided) may revoke licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and Compliance Officers (AMLCO) are individually criminally liable for failing to report suspicious transactions or executing payments for persons on sanctioned lists; travel bans, property seizure, personal fines, and imprisonment up to 10 years; civil liability for recovery of misappropriated funds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to submit the annual Form TD201 within 15 months of the tax year end or failing to pay provisional tax instalments on 31 July and 31 December; continuing position across subsequent years with outstanding returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed penalty of EUR 100 per un-filed return; where returns outstanding for consecutive years, EUR 200 per return; late payment interest at 1.75% per quarter and a 10% additional tax for unpaid tax at due date; removal of ability to obtain a tax clearance/certificate; restriction imposed on carrying forward tax losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under s. 43 of Assessment and Collection of Taxes Law, the directors of a company are jointly and severally liable for tax debts if the company's failure occurs after winding up proceedings or during a distraint; personal insolvency procedure may be instigated; refusal of travel clearance for outward movement.
